title: Apple App Store sales tax: A guide for US developers
summary: Learn what Apple handles for App Store tax and what developers must check: tax categories, forms, direct sales, reports, and state registration duties.
body_markdown:
For App Store transactions where Apple has the duty to collect and remit tax, developers should not collect the same tax again. Your work is to provide correct product and tax details, review the agreement for each market, and reconcile the reports.


That does not make Apple responsible for every sale your business makes. Direct website sales and other payment arrangements need their own review.


## Who is this guide for?


This guide is for US developers selling apps, subscriptions, or in-app purchases. If you are a customer asking why an App Store receipt includes tax, check the product, billing location, and receipt with Apple. There is no single App Store tax rate that applies to every buyer.


Do not change a billing address to claim a location that is not yours.


## What Apple handles and what you handle


Task What to check


Tax collection on an App Store transaction Apple's role under the current agreement and market rules


App and in-app purchase classification Your tax category settings


Developer tax identity Required forms and accurate legal entity details


Direct sales outside the store Your own collection and filing duties


Accounting Sales, tax, fees, refunds, and payouts reconciled separately


Apple's[current developer agreements](https://developer.apple.com/support/terms/) set the contractual scope. Avoid treating “merchant of record” as a blanket answer for every country and payment path.


## Set the right tax category


Apple's[tax category guide](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-app-information/set-a-tax-category/) explains that tax calculation uses the selected category along with app details, entity status, customer attributes, and local rules.


Choose the category that describes the product. You can use a separate category for an in-app purchase when appropriate. A category change affects future transactions, so do not assume it corrects prior charges.


Review the setting when the app changes from a software tool into an offering that also sells content or another product.


## Keep developer tax information current


Complete the required forms for your legal entity and relevant markets in App Store Connect. Apple's[tax information guide](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-tax-information/provide-tax-information/) explains the country-specific requirements and how to request corrections.


Apple prompts US-based developers to complete **Form W-9** . Have the business's legal tax name and the applicable taxpayer identification number, such as an EIN, ready. Follow[Apple's tax-information steps](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/manage-tax-information/provide-tax-information/) for the account's entity type.


Tax on customer purchases, tax on Apple's fees, and withholding from developer proceeds are different items. Keep them separate in the accounting review.


## International VAT and GST: check the country and entity


Apple's[paid-application schedules](https://developer.apple.com/support/downloads/terms/schedules/Schedule-2-and-3-English.pdf) refer to Exhibit B for responsibility for collecting and remitting transaction taxes. Read the version that applies to your account, including the country notes and developer-location conditions.


For each material market, record the customer country, selling entity, payment path, who collects, and any forms or registrations your business needs. Recheck that decision before routing sales through a new foreign subsidiary or enabling a different checkout. A country appearing in a coverage list is not enough to settle every entity and transaction.


Also keep tax on Apple's fees separate from tax on the buyer's purchase. Save the fee invoice and have the accountant assess any deduction or recoverable input tax under the applicable rules.


## Do marketplace sales remove state registration duties?


Not always. Review each state's rules for marketplace sales, direct sales, physical presence, and reporting. Do not assume you must register everywhere simply because a sales total crossed a number, or that platform collection removes every filing duty.


Keep a channel report that distinguishes tax Apple handled from tax your company collected. If you already have a state account, confirm the required returns before stopping filings. Use the[state sales tax guides](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/SaaS-sales-tax-guide) to review direct and marketplace sales for each location.


## What about payments outside Apple's purchase flow?


Review the exact terms and payment path. A transaction that occurs outside the covered store flow may leave collection and invoice duties with you or another seller.


Do this review before enabling the flow. Keep the customer receipt and tax records consistent with the party that actually handled the sale.


## Reconcile App Store proceeds


Start with the sales and financial reports, then identify refunds, taxes, fees, currency effects, and the resulting payout. A net deposit is not the same as gross sales or recognized revenue. A[SaaS chart of accounts](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/chart-of-accounts) helps keep the sales, tax, fees, and settlement amounts separate.


Keep the original reports and match the settlement to the bank. Apply your revenue policy separately;[usage-based revenue recognition](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/usage-based-pricing-guide) explains why billing and cash do not alone determine revenue.


## Download the reports behind the payout


In App Store Connect, open **Reports → Create Reports** , select the fiscal month and locations, create the report, then download it when ready. For transaction tax, select **Transaction Tax Report** in the report menu. Follow Apple's[report download instructions](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/getting-paid/download-financial-reports) for the required role and current steps.


The transaction tax report covers the US and Canada. Its[field definitions](https://developer.apple.com/help/app-store-connect/reference/reporting/transaction-tax-report-fields) identify the jurisdiction, tax category, rate, tax-exclusive amount, and taxes paid. It does not replace the financial report for withholding, input taxes, or other adjustments.


For each month, save:


- The financial report, transaction tax report, and bank settlement.
- Refunds and adjustments linked to their original transactions.
- Tax and fee invoices, including any tax on Apple's service fee.
- The tax-category decision and date of any change.
- Relevant registrations, returns, and notices.


Use those records to reconcile the payout and support the state-by-state review. Do not treat a net bank deposit as a complete sales report.


## What should you review each month?


Check for tax notices and agreement changes, new sales channels, changed product categories, and report differences. Apple's[tax and price updates](https://developer.apple.com/news/?id=artln8br) show why a fixed worldwide country list can become stale.


For Android sales, use the separate[Google Play tax guide](https://www.afternoon.co/blog/google-play-sales-tax-guide) . The platforms' responsibilities are not interchangeable.
